# Activity: Data Intake Card {.unnumbered}

## Goal

Students practice evaluating whether a health dataset is usable, ethical, documented, and appropriate for reproducible analysis.

## Approved Starter Portals (choose one)

Choose **one** dataset/indicator page from one of the portals below (pick something you care about).
You are **not** required to use the same dataset as other students.

1) **Survey-style microdata (person-level):** NHANES or NHIS (see Reference: Data Sources)  
   - Good if you want person-level variables (age, sex, BMI, smoking, etc.)
   - Expect: codebooks, sampling notes, and data dictionaries

2) **Indicators (aggregated country/province-level): WHO Global Health Observatory (GHO)**  
   - Good if you want country-level trends (life expectancy, mortality, vaccination coverage, etc.)
   - Expect: “indicator metadata” (definition + method), downloadable CSV, **not** person-level records

   **How to use GHO quickly (what to click):**
   - Pick **one indicator** (e.g., “Life expectancy at birth”, “Maternal mortality ratio”, “Diabetes prevalence”)
   - Pick **one geography** (Canada or another country/region)
   - Find: indicator definition / metadata, time coverage, and the download option

3) **Canadian open data portal:** BC Data Catalogue or Open Government Portal (Canada)  
   - Good if you want Canadian administrative/open datasets
   - Expect: variable definitions vary widely (sometimes excellent, sometimes minimal)

> Tip: If you’re unsure whether your selection is microdata or aggregated indicators, write “unknown” in `data_level` and explain what you observed on the download page.

## Student Template

```yaml
dataset_name: ""
publisher_org: ""
permalink_url: ""
date_accessed: "YYYY-MM-DD"
license_terms: ""
geography: ""
time_coverage: ""
data_level: ""   # microdata / aggregated / unknown
variables_of_interest:
  - name: ""
    definition: ""
known_limitations:
  - ""
stewardship_notes: ""
ai_use_note: ""
```

## Example (Completed Data Intake Card — sample)

### WHO

This example uses **one WHO indicator** to demonstrate what “Complete” looks like.
You may choose a different portal and topic.

```yaml
dataset_name: "Life expectancy at birth (years)"
publisher_org: "World Health Organization (WHO)"
permalink_url: "https://www.who.int/data/gho"
license_terms: "See WHO terms on the portal; record as provided"
geography: "Canada (and global comparison)"
time_coverage: "2000–2023 (varies by country)"
data_level: "Aggregated indicators (country-level)"
variables_of_interest:
  - name: "Life expectancy at birth (years)"
    definition: "Expected years of life at birth (method described in WHO metadata)"
    known_limitations: "Model-based estimates; depends on reporting quality; not person-level"
stewardship_notes: "No individual-level data; still avoid overclaiming causality; cite metadata."
ai_use_note: "Used AI to draft a plain-language summary of the indicator; verified against WHO metadata page."
```

### NHANES

```yaml
dataset_name: "NHANES 2017–2018 Demographics (example)"
publisher_org: "CDC / NCHS"
permalink_url: "https://wwwn.cdc.gov/nchs/nhanes/"
date_accessed: "YYYY-MM-DD"
license_terms: "Public-use (see NHANES guidance on site)"
geography: "United States"
time_coverage: "2017–2018"
data_level: "Microdata (person-level)"
variables_of_interest:
  - name: "RIAGENDR"
    definition: "Gender (coded categories per documentation)"
known_limitations:
  - "Complex survey design; weights needed for population inference"
stewardship_notes: "De-identified public-use microdata; still avoid reporting small cell counts."
ai_use_note: "Used AI to summarize the codebook section for RIAGENDR; verified against official documentation."
```

## Completion Checklist (Complete / Incomplete)

To be marked **Complete**, your card must include:

- [ ] A stable link (or link + date accessed)
- [ ] Publisher/organization named
- [ ] License/terms noted (even if “see portal terms”)
- [ ] Data level identified (microdata vs aggregated indicators)
- [ ] At least **one** variable with a definition grounded in documentation (not AI guesswork)
- [ ] One limitation or risk of misuse (privacy, over-interpretation, stewardship)
- [ ] AI-use note (what you used AI for + how you verified)

> If you’re uncertain about something, write **unknown** and explain what you looked for.

## Reproducibility Check

- The dataset link is stable or includes an access date.
- The publisher and license are named.
- Variable definitions come from source documentation, not AI guesses.
- The student records what they asked AI and how they verified the answer.
